title: Analysis of the Genesis of Shale Gas in the Southern Ordos Basin: Based on Geochemical Evidence
content:
Shale gas has been found in the Mesozoic Yanchang Formation in the southern Ordos Basin over recent years. To date, however, whether its gas source rocks are dominated by coalbed methane, biogas, or shallow associated gas has not been examined systematically. In this contribution, the genesis of Mesozoic shale gas in the southern Ordos Basin is investigated by contrasting the geochemical signatures—gas composition and carbon isotopes—of several genetic gas types, namely Mesozoic shale gas, Mesozoic shallow gas, Upper Paleozoic natural gas, and biogenic gas from neighbouring basins.
For the Mesozoic shale gas in the southern Ordos Basin, methane content lies between 46.08% and 94.56%, heavy hydrocarbon content between 2.86% and 37.61%, and methane carbon isotope values between −52.0‰ and −46.4‰. On the basis of comparative analysis of gas components and carbon isotopes, it is concluded that the Yanchang Formation shale gas of the Ordos Basin is neither Upper Paleozoic coal-type gas nor biogenic gas; instead, its geochemical fingerprint resembles that of shallow gas within the basin, and it represents a crude oil-associated gas generated by pyrolysis of sapropelic-type source rocks in the Yanchang Formation. Accordingly, the shale gas of the Mesozoic Yanchang Formation in the Ordos Basin is identified as pyrolytic gas whose source rocks can only be the Yanchang Formation itself. These findings offer theoretical support for shale gas exploration in the southern part of the basin.
